sections.html:
Reynoldsburg is a Columbus suburb with a large retail base and a mix of owners and renters. Population is 43,350 by the July 2025 estimate, 5.5% above the 2020 base of 41,074, living on 11.12 square miles of land in 17,280 households. Owners occupy 61.6% of homes, the midpoint value is $244,300 and the midpoint rent is $1,259.

Buyers often filter listings by school, so name the elementary and junior high that serve the street, but confirm the attendance zone with the district first. A listing can also point to nearby shopping and a manageable drive without naming a subdivision.

The city reaches into Franklin, Fairfield and Licking counties, each with a separate auditor and treasurer. Council legislation from 2026 mentions a Taylor Road annexation in Etna Township and Summit Road work shared with Licking County, so a parcel near that edge may answer to a different office.

In practice, the clerk certifies nuisance costs to both the Franklin County Auditor and the Licking County Auditor for collection, and the city certifies its tax levies to both. If the city ever billed you for cleanup on the lot, ask which county auditor holds the charge before closing.

The Building Division administers four codes, Ohio Building, Residential, Property Maintenance and Flood Damage Prevention, plus the National Electrical Code. It issues certificates of occupancy and permits for building, electrical, heating, plumbing, sign, sidewalk and flood hazard work. It sits at 7232 East Main Street and answers at 614-322-6802.

  • Residential plan review starts with a permit application, construction drawings and a $100 non-refundable deposit.
  • Plumbing plan review and inspection run through Franklin County Public Health, at 280 East Broad Street in Columbus, not through the city.
  • Contractors register each year with a $75 fee, proof of liability coverage of at least $500,000 and a state license where one applies.
  • Inspections requested by 3 p.m. through the automated line, 614-322-6821, are generally done the next business day, though the city has up to four days.

Inspectors working for buyers tend to ask about permits for decks, basement finishes and plumbing changes, so gather those records early.

The city's 2026 legislation list includes an ordinance to establish Section 705, Permitting Short-Term Rentals, as a chapter of the codified ordinances. An owner who rents a house by the night and wants to sell it to another host should ask the city whether any permit passes to a new owner.

The same list shows a council action in 2026 to expand the Eastern Community Reinvestment Area, which allows property tax abatement, and several agreements for tax exemption on new projects. Ask the city whether your address sits inside an abatement district before you tell a buyer an abatement is available.

A short list of calls and records can shorten the sale, whichever route you choose.

  • Confirm the county on your tax bill and the date of the next installment.
  • Pull permits for every deck, basement, furnace or plumbing change, and ask Franklin County Public Health about any plumbing approval.
  • Ask the Building Department about open code violation notices or citations on the address.
  • Check for a nuisance charge that the city sent to the county auditor.
  • Write down which Reynoldsburg elementary and junior high serve the street.

These answers also help a direct buyer make a firmer offer, because fewer unknowns remain at the closing table.

sections.h2: How the sale moves from contract to closing
sections.html:
Whichever route you take, the steps run in roughly the same order. Once a buyer is under contract, the title company searches the record for liens, nuisance charges certified to a county auditor and open permits. If the search turns up an unclosed permit for a deck, a basement finish or a furnace swap, the Building Division is the office that can tell you what an inspection would take. Remember that inspections requested through the automated line by 3 p.m. are generally done the next business day, though the city has up to four days, so build that cushion into your closing date.

Plumbing work adds a second office. Plans and inspections for plumbing go through Franklin County Public Health in Columbus, so a plumbing change made without approval needs a call there, not to city hall. After the paperwork is clean, the settlement agent splits the current tax bill between you and the buyer, collects any amount past due from your proceeds, and records the deed with the county that bills your parcel. Because the city touches three counties, ask the title company early which county that is.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html: If you visit or call the Building Division, have the street address, the parcel number and any permit numbers you can find. Say plainly what you are trying to learn: whether a certificate of occupancy is on file, whether permits were closed, and whether any code notice or citation is open. For tax questions, the parcel number is the key detail for the Treasurer at 614-525-3438. For a nuisance charge, ask which county auditor, Franklin or Licking, holds the certified amount, since the clerk sends such costs to both. Write down the name of anyone you speak with and the date, and keep the answers with your closing papers so a buyer or title company can see them.

sections.h2: Franklin County tax bills on a sale
sections.html:
Franklin County collects in two halves each year, and payments after the second-half due date carry penalty and interest. Call the Treasurer at 614-525-3438 for the amount owed on a given parcel and the current dates. Values are reset on a six-year cycle with a midpoint update, and between cycles they move only for physical changes, demolition or a Board of Revision ruling.

An owner disputing the 2026 value can file with the Auditor from November 20, 2026 until March 31, 2027. Qualifying owners who are 65, disabled or certain surviving spouses may use the Homestead credit, and the Auditor's decision follows verification that total income does not exceed $41,000.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale right for you?
sections.html:
Owners with deferred repairs, an unclosed permit or a departing tenant often pick a cash sale, because they value a set closing date over a long listing period. A buyer with a loan brings an appraisal and an inspection, and either can delay a sale or prompt repair requests.

Direct buyers typically take the house as is. Get each offer in writing, learn who pays closing costs and read the settlement statement before signing day.

faqs.a: Reynoldsburg lies in Franklin, Fairfield and Licking counties. Check your parcel to see which county auditor and treasurer bill your property.

faqs.q: Who handles plumbing permits in Reynoldsburg?
faqs.a: Franklin County Public Health reviews plumbing plans and schedules plumbing inspections for the city. Once a plan is approved, the permit application goes to the city's Building Division.

The city's 2026 legislation list includes an ordinance establishing Section 705, Permitting Short-Term Rentals. Ask the city for the current permit rules before listing a house that is used as a rental.

faqs.q: What happens if a Franklin County tax payment is late?
faqs.a: After the second-half due date the Treasurer adds penalty and interest, and not receiving a bill does not change that. Call 614-525-3438 for the amount owed on your parcel.
The 2020 to 2024 count is 17,280 households with 2.38 people each on average. Roughly 61.6% are owned by the people living in them.
